retiredFleetSkills.name: repocontext
retiredFleetSkills.reason: The skill's entire contract is 'exactly eight read-only, job-oriented tools' served by an MCP server named repocontext. No such server exists anywhere on the fleet, so the skill names tools that cannot be called.
retiredFleetSkills.evidence: registry/mcps.json declares twelve servers and repocontext is not among them. All 17 readable host MCP configs were enumerated and none registers it -- codex's config mentions the string only in a stale [projects.'c:\repos\shmindmaster\repocontext'] trust entry, which is a project-trust row, not a server. Both routes the skill documents are dead: the local stdio route runs `pnpm --dir C:/Repos/shmindmaster/repocontext mcp:serve` and that directory does not exist (C:/Repos/shmindmaster holds 18 repos, none named repocontext), and the remote route needs a REPOCONTEXT_MCP_TOKEN no host holds. Deployed to 14 hosts at retirement.
retiredFleetSkills.whyFleetScoped: repowise supersedes it but maps to 8 hosts, only 5 of which overlap the 14 carrying repocontext. A capability-scoped retirement would have cleaned 5, left 9, and reported success.
retiredFleetSkills.corroboratingResidue: A whole-disk sweep (not just the skills directories) also found ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp/repocontext and ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/mcp/repocontext. These are antigravity's own tool-description caches, holding exactly the eight tools the skill documents -- repo.compare, repo.inspect, repo.read, repo.search, wiki.analyze, wiki.catalog, wiki.get, wiki.search -- each with parameters: null. They are stale caches from when repocontext WAS registered, and antigravity's live mcp_config.json does not list it, so they corroborate the retirement rather than contradicting it. Deliberately NOT swept: they are a host's internal cache, not a managed skill, and are the host's to regenerate.

hostMappings.deploymentStatusNote: Loose skills, not the plugin, since 2026-08-20 -- and this is the SECOND capability to hit this exact failure. The plugin is disabled on claude because claude ships its own browser surface, so routing to a native capability beats spawning a local server. But the plugin was also claude's only source for browser-debugging, browser-evidence, interactive-browser-testing and use-playwright-mcp, so disabling it left claude with NO browser guidance at all while this mapping still read native-plugin-installed. Skills carry no process cost and are useful with a native browser -- their first resolution step is to use the host's own browser -- so they deploy independently of the MCP. The same split already applies to mobile-development; the general rule is that a plugin bundling skills+MCP cannot be disabled to gate the MCP without first moving its skills to loose deployment.
